Commentary.Commentary: We are back for India's reply with the bat! The umpires are out in the middle and the openers for India, Sanju Samson and Abhishek Sharma stride out first. Now come in the England players who are spreading across the field to take their positions. Jofra Archer has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings. Away we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

With just 172 runs required for India to clinch the series tonight, the pitch looks perfect for batting, and with the dew likely to settle in, the chase shouldn't pose much of a challenge. England, however, face a must-win scenario and will need to dig deep, relying on disciplined bowling and unwavering belief to pull off this tough defence. The chase gets underway shortly so stay tuned!

From a commanding position at 83/1, England spiralled into chaos, collapsing to 127/8 in no time as Varun Chakravarthy cast a spell with his mesmerizing spin, claiming wickets almost at will. His breathtaking five-wicket haul stood out as the defining moment of the innings. Liam Livingstone offered a glimmer of resistance, unleashing a few towering hits against Ravi Bishnoi to reignite some hope for his side. However, his charge was abruptly halted by Hardik Pandya’s timely return to the attack. England however managed to scrape through their 20 overs with a strong 24-run partnership for the 10th wicket but could only muster a respectable total, leaving much to be desired given their early dominance.

After the early dismissal of Phil Salt, Ben Duckett took charge, igniting England’s innings with a flurry of boundaries. Partnering with Jos Buttler, the duo looked comfortable as they built a promising 76-run stand, seamlessly countering both pace and spin. However, the tide turned dramatically when Varun Chakravarthy broke through by removing the in-form Buttler, and Axar Pate followed suit by dismissing Duckett shortly after his well-crafted half-century. What followed was a collapse of epic proportions.

It’s been another stellar display of spin bowling from the Indian attack, masterfully spearheaded by Varun Chakravarthy, to hold England to a modest total of 171 runs. At one point, England seemed well on track for a towering score, potentially surpassing 200. However, a dramatic middle-order collapse brought their charge to a screeching halt leaving them with much to ponder as they head into the break.

Oh, the throw has caught Mark Wood on the back and England will get a couple of runs to end the innings. A low full toss on middle, Wood clears the front leg and hammers it down to long on and the batters straightaway think about two runs. Wood turns back after the single and Jurel's throw from long on hits his back and he is able to make it. England finish with 171/9 on the board!

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! What a turnaround for India! Just when Jos Buttler and Ben Duckett were threatening to take the game away, India have struck gold, removing both set batters in quick succession, flipping the momentum back in their favour. Losing two big wickets within 7 balls is a massive blow for England, especially after such a strong start. Now, England will need to rebuild carefully while ensuring they don’t lose sight of the aggressive intent they started with. For India, this is the perfect opportunity to tighten the screws. Their spinners, who’ve been phenomenal in the middle overs throughout this series, will now look to pile on the pressure and force England into further mistakes. Also, Liam Livingstone walks out to bat now.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Sanju Samson has gone up in celebration and is certain that there is an edge on that one but the umpire disagrees. Not much excitement from the bowler either but Suryakumar Yadav does opt for the review. Varun Chakravarthy fires this one in fuller and around off, the ball skids through. Jos Buttler goes for the reverse sweep but fails to connect and the ball just sneaks under the willow. Samson with a sharp low take and the third umpire is called in. UltraEdge takes some time to build up and shows that there is a clear spike when the ball is next to the bat and the decision is overturned. A huge review and India have the big fish! Even Kevin Pietersen, one of the on-air commentators read Buttler's look of guilt as the check was going on.

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the game to begin! The umpires are out in the middle and the Indian players have taken their places on the field. It will be the duo of Phil Salt and Ben Duckett to open the innings for England yet again. And, it will be the returning Mohammed Shami who will start proceedings with the new ball. Let's play...

Jos Buttler, the skipper of England says that it looks like a really good surface and they will now look to bat well. Mentions that they would have opted to bowl first as well had they won the toss. States that they have to be at their best and put up a good performance. Informs that Jamie Smith has a calf strain and hence, he will keep wickets for them.

Suryakumar Yadav, the captain of India says that they will bowl first and the pitch looks nice and hard and won't change much. Mentions that Rajkot generally has been a good track and it should play well. Adds that they wanted to play a different brand of cricket and Tilak Varma really bailed them out last time. Adds that they are now looking at it as a three-game series and want to play accordingly and goes on to inform that Mohammed Shami is in for Arshdeep Singh who has been rested.
England (Unchanged Playing XI) - Phil Salt, Ben Duckett, Jos Buttler (C), Harry Brook, Liam Livingstone, Jamie Smith (WK), Jamie Overton, Brydon Carse, Jofra Archer, Adil Rashid, Mark Wood.

India (Playing XI) - Sanju Samson (WK), Abhishek Sharma, Suryakumar Yadav (C), Tilak Varma, Hardik Pandya, Dhruv Jurel, Washington Sundar, Axar Patel, Ravi Bishnoi, Mohammed Shami (in for Arshdeep Singh), Varun Chakravarthy.
TOSS UPDATE - India have won the coin flip and will BOWL first.

For England, it has been a series of missed opportunities. Jos Buttler has been the lone warrior in the batting department, standing tall while the rest of the lineup has struggled to tackle India’s spinners. Their express pace duo of Mark Wood and Jofra Archer looked menacing upfront but lost steam at the death, something they will need to rectify if they want to restrict India’s power-packed batting lineup. England’s key challenge remains countering spin, which has consistently tied them down in both games. Despite their struggles, they’ve stuck to their guns and announced an unchanged XI, reflecting their confidence in turning things around. With the series on the line for England and India aiming to wrap things up, expect a fiery contest here. The Toss and team updates are just moments away so stay tuned.

India, the reigning T20 World Cup champions, have been in stellar form with a record of 15 wins in their last 17 T20Is. Their bold, aggressive, and fearless approach under new leadership has been widely praised. India’s spinners have played a pivotal role in the series so far, delivering breakthroughs at critical junctures, but what has stood out is the team’s overall balance and cohesion. All eyes will be on whether Mohammed Shami makes his much-anticipated return to the XI, but the team might manage his workload carefully with bigger assignments ahead.

Hello and a warm welcome to our coverage of the third T20I of this 5-match series between India and England, coming to you from Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot! With India leading the series 2-0, they’ll look to seal the series tonight, while England will be fighting tooth and nail to stay alive in the contest. After a nail-biting finish in the second game, there's a lot to play for as both teams gear up for another high-stakes clash.

After a nail-biting finish in the second T20I and India leading the 5-match series 2-0, the stage is set for a crucial third T20I at the Niranjan Shah Stadium in Rajkot. With the stakes sky-high, England must pull off a victory to keep the series alive, while India will aim to continue their dominance and seal the series with two matches to spare. The visitors come into this match with renewed confidence after a spirited fight in the second game. Their batting unit, while still over-reliant on Jos Buttler, showed better resistance to spin, and Brydon Carse shone as a standout performer with both bat and ball. England’s pacers impressed early on, troubling the Indian batters, but they lacked discipline and consistency in the death overs. To stay in contention, England have named the same XI for this game and will need a complete performance. On the other hand, India’s fearless brand of cricket has been the hallmark of their success in this series. Even in the second game, when the odds were against them, their batters showed no hesitation in playing their shots, exemplifying the team’s attacking mindset under the new setup. Their batting lineup remains formidable, and their spinners have been exceptional, consistently deceiving England’s batters. The potential inclusion of Mohammed Shami, making his long-awaited return, adds an exciting dimension to India’s bowling attack, which has so far relied on Arshdeep Singh as their sole frontline pacer. With England’s backs against the wall, they are expected to leave no stone unturned, while India will look to capitalize on their momentum, especially at home, and clinch the series. Both teams are primed for a thrilling contest, and all eyes are on Rajkot as this pivotal game unfolds. Who will rise to the occasion? We shall soon find out!
